topic: What if you could move at double speed?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
MOVE AT DOUBLE SPEED?

power.rule: you switch to twice your speed for as long as you like; the world stays at normal speed
power.look: a 2x chip, the picture cools and sharpens, speed streaks trail the hero; everyone else looks slowed

script.beat: 1 cold open, demo 1 (small and selfish; tool-reel 'so' clause: a negative outcome removed)
script.text: Your mug slips. Double. Caught, so it never hits the floor.
Mo races you upstairs. Double. You're already waiting at the top.
Double again. The whole class freezes mid-blink.
What if you could move at double speed?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: air pushes back with the square of your speed. Twice as fast, four times the push. That's real.

script.beat: 5-7 folded into a question (tool-reel: a closing line that pulls comments)
script.text: So what happens when you trip?

science.claim: Air pushes back with the square of your speed: twice as fast, four times the push.
science.working: The drag equation: F = 1/2 x rho x v^2 x Cd x A. Air density rho, the drag coefficient Cd and the frontal area A stay the same when only the speed changes, so F scales with v^2. Doubling v: (2v)^2 = 4 v^2, four times the drag force. (At running speeds air drag on a person is turbulent, quadratic drag, which is the regime this law describes.)
science.source: The drag equation (NASA Glenn Research Center, 'The Drag Equation'); standard fluid dynamics
